title: Finetuning: 500m AI agents in production with 2 engineers — Mustafa Ali & Kyle Corbitt
talk_summary: Method scaled a liability-data extraction agent to 500M requests using GPT-4, hit $70k/month and prompt-engineering walls, then fine-tuned an 8B Llama 3.1 on production data distilled from a stronger teacher model to beat GPT-4 on error rate, latency, and cost. OpenPipe's core advice is to benchmark real production models on error rate/latency/cost first, and only fine-tune when prompting can't hit thresholds.

takeaways.technique: Benchmark models on error rate, latency, and cost under production conditions before choosing
takeaways.what_they_do: They measure each candidate model's error rate against human-verified ground truth, plus latency and real cost (including reasoning tokens), on a diverse production-like task mix at realistic concurrency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you also want to make sure that you're using real production conditions that you're actually doing um you know like a real diversity of tasks
takeaways.numbers: GPT-4 ~11% error, o3-mini ~4% error; GPT-4 ~1s latency, o3-mini ~5s; o3-mini costlier than GPT-4o despite lower per-token price due to reasoning tokens

takeaways.technique: Distill a strong teacher into a small cheap model via fine-tuning
takeaways.what_they_do: They generate outputs on production inputs using a strong model (o3-mini) and fine-tune an 8B Llama 3.1 on those pairs, getting close to teacher quality at far lower latency and cost.
takeaways.numbers: 8B Llama 3.1 beat GPT-4 on error rate and far exceeded cost thresholds; smaller model gives lower latency due to fewer sequential layers

takeaways.technique: Track real cost including reasoning tokens, not sticker price
takeaways.what_they_do: They compute actual per-task cost rather than per-token list price, revealing that a cheaper-per-token reasoning model was more expensive overall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 03 mini even though it has a much lower per token cost than GPD 40 ... we found it was a little bit more expensive because it ... generates many more reasoning tokens
takeaways.numbers: o3-mini more expensive than GPT-4o for their task despite lower per-token price

takeaways.technique: Recognize prompt-engineering ceiling and switch strategy
takeaways.what_they_do: They hit a wall where fixing a prompt for one case broke another, with no prompt versioning, and concluded prompting alone couldn't generalize.

takeaways.technique: Post-hoc plausibility checks as a second gate
takeaways.what_they_do: Method runs extra checks after the model output to see if results are plausible and match expected patterns, so they don't need 0% model error.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they have um extra checks that happen after this where they look and see okay are the numbers that came out plausible
takeaways.numbers: ~9% error rate was acceptable given downstream checks
